content.text: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) if you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

content.label: Damage Resistance
content.text: You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

content.label: Rage Damage
content.text: When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike)—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

content.label: Strength Advantage
content.text: You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

content.label: No Concentration or Spells
content.text: You can't maintain [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration), and you can't cast spells.

content.label: Duration
content.text: The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

items.text: Make an attack roll against an enemy.
Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
Take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to extend your Rage.

content.text: Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

While you aren't wearing any armor, your base [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield) and still gain this benefit.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as [Greataxes](srd-5.2/06/weapons/greataxe) and [Handaxes](srd-5.2/06/weapons/handaxe). Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition.

You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) during that time.

You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.
You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: [Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics), [Intimidation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/intimidation), [Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception), [Stealth](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/stealth), or [Survival](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/survival). When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.
Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.
Your instincts are so honed that you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) rolls.
As part of the [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed).

If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage). If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

content.label: Forceful Blow
content.text: The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) straight toward the target without provoking [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks).

content.label: Hamstring Blow
content.text: The target's [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time—the most recent one.

Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), the DC resets to 10.
You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

content.label: Staggering Blow
content.text: The target has [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks) until the start of your next turn.

content.label: Sundering Blow
content.text: Before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll. An attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus.

When you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative), you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the [Unconscious](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unconscious) condition (not just the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition) or don Heavy armor.
The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to 2d10. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.
If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Irresistible Offense](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-irresistible-offense) is recommended.
You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.
As a Barbarian, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Barbarian levels. These features are listed in the Barbarian Features table.

If you use Reckless Attack while your Rage is active, you deal extra damage to the first target you hit on your turn with a Strength-based attack. To determine the extra damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. The damage has the same type as the weapon or [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike) used for the attack.

You have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) and [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) conditions while your Rage is active. If you're [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) or [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) when you enter your Rage, the condition ends on you.

When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike).

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can strike terror into others with your menacing presence and primal power. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency)). On a failed save, a creature has the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Berserker direct their Rage primarily toward violence. Their path is one of untrammeled fury, and they thrill in the chaos of battle as they allow their Rage to seize and empower them.

content.text: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6.

content.label: Using Bardic Inspiration
content.text: As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Once within the next hour when the creature fails a [D20 Test](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test), the creature can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.

content.label: Number of Uses
content.text: You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: At Higher Levels
content.text: Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain Bard levels, as shown in the Bardic Die column of the Bard Features table. The die becomes a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the Bard spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list. *[Dancing Lights](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dancing-lights)* and *[Vicious Mockery](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/vicious-mockery)* are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list.
When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Bard spell list. *[Charm Person](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/charm-person)*, *[Color Spray](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/color-spray)*, *[Dissonant Whispers](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dissonant-whispers)*, and *[Healing Word](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/healing-word)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Bard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Bard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Bard spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use a [Musical Instrument](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/musical-instrument) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Bard spells.

You gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. [Performance](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/performance) and [Persuasion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/persuasion) are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Bard level 9, you gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

You can add half your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency) (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency).

For example, if you make a Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check and lack [Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics) proficiency, you can add half your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency) to the check.

Does your Bard beat a [drum](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/musical-instrument) while chanting the deeds of ancient heroes? Strum a [lute](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/musical-instrument) while crooning romantic tunes? Perform arias of stirring power? Recite dramatic monologues from classic tragedies? Use the rhythm of a folk dance to coordinate the movement of allies in battle? Compose naughty limericks?

When you play a Bard, consider the style of artistic performance you favor, the moods you might invoke, and the themes that inspire your own creations. Are your poems inspired by moments of natural beauty, or are they brooding reflections on loss? Do you prefer lofty hymns or rowdy tavern songs? Are you drawn to laments for the fallen or celebrations of joy? Do you dance merry jigs or perform elaborate interpretive choreography? Do you focus on one style of performance or strive to master them all?

You gain a Bard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Bard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Bard level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Bard levels 8, 12, and 16.
You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) or [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage).

You've learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you (see a class's section for its spell list). In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.
When you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative), you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Spell Recall](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-spell-recall) is recommended.

You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the *[Power Word Heal](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/power-word-heal)* and *[Power Word Kill](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/power-word-kill)* spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.
As a Bard, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Bard levels. These features are listed in the Bard Features table.

This section presents the Bard spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.
You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

You learn to use your wit to supernaturally distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others. When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll, reducing the damage or potentially turning the success into a failure.

You learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof (see a class's section for its spell list). A spell you choose must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Bard Features table.
You always have the chosen spells prepared, and whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of the spells with another spell that meets these requirements.

When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failure into a success. On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended.

Bards of the College of Lore collect spells and secrets from diverse sources, such as scholarly tomes, mystical rites, and peasant tales. The college's members gather in libraries and universities to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.

content.text: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Cleric spells, which appear on the Cleric spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list. *[Guidance](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/guidance)*, *[Sacred Flame](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/sacred-flame)*, and *[Thaumaturgy](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/thaumaturgy)* are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Cleric spell list.
When you reach Cleric levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Cleric spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Cleric Features table.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Cleric spell list. *[Bless](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/bless)*, *[Cure Wounds](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/cure-wounds)*, *[Guiding Bolt](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/guiding-bolt)*, and *[Shield of Faith](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/shield-of-faith)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Cleric levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Cleric Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Cleric spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Cleric, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Cleric feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Cleric spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Cleric spells for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use a [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Cleric spells.
Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana) or [Religion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/religion)) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you point your [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) at another creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself and focus divine energy at it. Roll 1d8 and add your Wisdom modifier. You either restore [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to the creature equal to that total or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to that total. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage (round down).
You roll an additional d8 when you reach Cleric levels 7 (2d8), 13 (3d8), and 18 (4d8).

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you present your [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) and censure Undead creatures. Each Undead of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its save, it has the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) and [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) conditions for 1 minute. For that duration, it tries to move as far from you as it can on its turns. This effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition, or if you die.

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, choose which Channel Divinity effect from this class to create. You gain additional effect options at higher Cleric levels.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). You gain additional uses when you reach certain Cleric levels, as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table.
If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Cleric levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Cleric level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful.

content.label: Divine Strike
content.text: The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8.

content.label: Potent Spellcasting
content.text: When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Fate](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-fate) is recommended.

You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.
As a Cleric, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Cleric levels. These features are listed in the Cleric Features table.

This section presents the Cleric spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.

Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Life Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to a creature, that creature regains additional [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) on the turn you cast the spell. The additional [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you present your [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to five times your Cleric level. Choose [Bloodied](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bloodied) creatures within 30 feet of yourself (which can include you), and divide those [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half its [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) maximum.

The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.

When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to a creature with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to a creature with a spell, you restore 12.
The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing, using that life force to cure many hurts.

Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

content.text: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the *[Speak with Animals](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/speak-with-animals)* spell prepared.

You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence ([Investigation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/investigation)) check but can't decipher it without magic.

You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana) or [Nature](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/nature)) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.
You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Druid spells, which appear on the Druid spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. *[Druidcraft](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/druidcraft)* and *[Produce Flame](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/produce-flame)* are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list.
When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Druid Features table.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Druid spell list. *[Animal Friendship](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/animal-friendship)*, *[Cure Wounds](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/cure-wounds)*, *[Faerie Fire](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/faerie-fire)*, and *[Thunderwave](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/thunderwave)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Druid Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Druid spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Druid, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Druid feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Druid spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells with other Druid spells for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use a [Druidic Focus](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/druidic-focus) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Druid spells.

You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the *[Find Familiar](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/find-familiar)* spell without Material components.
When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

content.label: Number of Uses
content.text: You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

content.label: Known Forms
content.text: You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum [Challenge Rating](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/challenge-rating) of 1/4 and that lack a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) (see appendix B for stat block options). The [Rat](srd-5.2/15/rat), [Riding Horse](srd-5.2/15/riding-horse), [Spider](srd-5.2/15/spider), and [Wolf](srd-5.2/15/wolf) are recommended. Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.

When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known forms and the maximum [Challenge Rating](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/challenge-rating) for those forms increases, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. In addition, starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed).
When choosing known forms, you may look in the System Reference Document or elsewhere for eligible Beasts if the Dungeon Master permits you to do so.

content.label: Rules While Shape-Shifted
content.text: While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

items.label: Temporary Hit Points
items.text: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) equal to your Druid level.

items.label: Game Statistics
items.text: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points); [Hit Point Dice](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-point-dice); Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency) for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.

items.label: No Spellcasting
items.text: You can't cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn't break your [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

items.label: Objects
items.text: Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

content.text: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Druid levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Druid level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, and 16.
Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required).

In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (choose when you hit).
The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

content.label: Potent Spellcasting
content.text: When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell's range increases by 300 feet.

While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits.

content.label: Evergreen Wild Shape
content.text: Whenever you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it.

content.label: Nature Magician
content.text: You can convert uses of Wild Shape into a spell slot (no action required). Choose a number of your unexpended uses of Wild Shape and convert them into a single spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels. For example, if you convert two uses of Wild Shape, you produce a level 4 spell slot. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Longevity
content.text: The primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.
As a Druid, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Druid levels. These features are listed in the Druid Features table.

This section presents the Druid spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.

Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), choose one type of land: arid, polar, temperate, or tropical. Consult the table below that corresponds to the chosen type; you have the spells listed for your Druid level and lower prepared.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Vitality-giving flowers and life-draining thorns appear for a moment in a 10-foot-radius [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) centered on that point. Each creature of your choice in the [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d6 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. One creature of your choice in that area regains 2d6 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points).
The damage and healing increase by 1d6 when you reach Druid levels 10 (3d6) and 14 (4d6).

You can cast one of the level 1+ spells that you have prepared from your Circle Spells feature without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) before you do so again.

In addition, when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your Druid level (round up), and none of them can be level 6+. For example, if you're a level 6 Druid, you can recover up to three levels' worth of spell slots. You can recover a level 3 spell slot, a level 2 and a level 1 spell slot, or three level 1 spell slots. Once you recover spell slots with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

You are immune to the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition, and you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to a damage type associated with your current land choice in the Circle Spells feature, as shown in the Nature's Ward table.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and cause spectral trees and vines to appear in a 15-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) on the ground within 120 feet of yourself. They last there for 1 minute or until you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition or die. You and your allies have [Half Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) while in that area, and your allies gain the current [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) of your Nature's Ward while there.
As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can move the [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) up to 60 feet to ground within 120 feet of yourself.

The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites. These Druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can use it to regain [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.

Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can move up to half your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) without provoking [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks).

If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

You can use this feature twice before a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) starting at level 13 and three times before a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) starting at level 17.

When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the [Push](srd-5.2/06/weapons/mastery-properties/push), [Sap](srd-5.2/06/weapons/mastery-properties/sap), or [Slow](srd-5.2/06/weapons/mastery-properties/slow) property for that attack.
You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.

You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

content.text: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a [Critical Hit](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/critical-hit) on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

Thanks to your athleticism, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) rolls and Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) checks.

content.text: You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [Death Saving Throws](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/death-saving-throw). A Champion focuses on the development of martial prowess in a relentless pursuit of victory. Champions combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, withstand peril, and garner glory. Whether in athletic contests or bloody battle, Champions strive for the crown of the victor.

You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the Grapple or Shove option of your [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to determine the save DC.
Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike) and Monk weapons, which are the following:

content.text: You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield).
While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield), your base [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.
You can expend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

You can take the [Disengage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disengage) action as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the [Disengage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disengage) and the [Dodge](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dodge) actions as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

You can take the [Dash](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dash) action as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the [Disengage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disengage) and [Dash](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dash) actions as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the Monk Features table.
You can expend these points to enhance or fuel certain Monk features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind, each of which is detailed below.

When you expend a Focus Point, it is unavailable until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), at the end of which you regain all your expended points.
Some features that use Focus Points require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency).

Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield). This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the Monk Features table.

When you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative), you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to reduce the attack's total damage against you. The reduction equals 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force. If you do so, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself if the attack was a melee attack or a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn't behind [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) if the attack was a ranged attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier. The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Monk level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, and 16.
You can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the [Stunned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/stunned) condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target's [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage).
Whenever you deal damage with your [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition.

While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield), you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.
Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits.

content.label: Flurry of Blows
content.text: You can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three Unarmed Strikes with it instead of two.

content.label: Patient Defense
content.text: When you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain a number of [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

content.label: Step of the Wind
content.text: When you expend a Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing creature within 5 feet of yourself that is Large or smaller. You move the creature with you until the end of your turn. The creature's movement doesn't provoke [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks).

Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed), [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened), or [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned).
In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of [Exhaustion](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/exhaustion).
You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.
Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.
When you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition. During that time, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to all damage except Force damage.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Irresistible Offense](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-irresistible-offense) is recommended.
You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

content.title: Monk Features

content.text: The target can't make [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks) until the start of its next turn.
The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you.
The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition.
Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target.

You gain the ability to heal yourself. As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) regained).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

When you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), you can expend 4 Focus Points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your Monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you take an action to end them. Alternatively, when you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn, you can forgo one of the attacks to end the vibrations. To end them, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you end them, the target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can end the vibrations harmlessly (no action required).
Warriors of the Open Hand are masters of unarmed combat. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents and manipulate their own energy to protect themselves from harm.

content.text: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). With that pool, you can restore a total number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to five times your Paladin level.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.

You can also expend 5 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) from the pool of healing power to remove the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition from the creature; those points don't also restore [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to the creature.

You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the Paladin spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Paladin Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Paladin spells. *[Heroism](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/heroism)* and *[Searing Smite](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/searing-smite)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Paladin levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Paladin Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Paladin spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Paladin Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use a [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Paladin spells.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as [Longswords](srd-5.2/06/weapons/longsword) and [Javelins](srd-5.2/06/weapons/javelin).

Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of [Halberds](srd-5.2/06/weapons/halberd) and [Flails](srd-5.2/06/weapons/flail).
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

You always have the *[Divine Smite](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/divine-smite)* spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) before you can cast it in this way again.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the *[Hallow](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/hallow)* spell.

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.
If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

You gain a Paladin subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Paladin level or lower.
A Paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most dedicated are fallible. Sometimes a Paladin transgresses their oath.
A Paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution, spending an all-night vigil as a sign of penitence or undertaking a fast. After a rite of forgiveness, the Paladin starts fresh.
If your Paladin unrepentantly violates their oath, talk to your DM. Your Paladin should probably take a more appropriate subclass or even abandon the class and adopt another one.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.
You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the *[Find Steed](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/find-steed)* spell prepared.
You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition.
You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
If another Paladin is present, a creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time; the creature chooses which aura while in them.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your [Holy Symbol](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-symbol) or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

You and your allies have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unarmed-strike), the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: [Blinded](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blinded), [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed), [Deafened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/deafened), [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened), [Paralyzed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/paralyzed), or [Stunned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/stunned). You must expend 5 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) from the healing pool of Lay On Hands for each of these conditions you remove; those points don't also restore [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) to the creature.
Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation).
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Truesight](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-truesight) is recommended.

content.text: This section presents the Paladin spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.

The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Devotion Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to imbue one Melee weapon that you are holding with positive energy. For 10 minutes or until you use this feature again, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls you make with that weapon (minimum bonus of +1), and each time you hit with it, you cause it to deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage.
The weapon also emits [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 20-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) 20 feet beyond that.
You can end this effect early (no action required). This effect also ends if you aren't carrying the weapon.

You and your allies have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

Your magical smite now radiates protective energy. Whenever you cast *[Divine Smite](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/divine-smite)*, you and your allies have [Half Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) while in your Aura of Protection. The aura has this benefit until the start of your next turn.
You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on any saving throw you are forced to make by a Fiend or an Undead.
Whenever an enemy starts its turn in the aura, that creature takes Radiant damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency).
The aura is filled with [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) that is sunlight.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can imbue your Aura of Protection with holy power, granting the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

The Oath of Devotion binds Paladins to the ideals of justice and order. These Paladins meet the archetype of the knight in shining armor. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some—for better or worse—hold the rest of the world to the same standards.

Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of personal devotion. Others hold angels as their ideals and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.
These paladins share the following tenets:

items.text: Let your word be your promise.
Protect the weak and never fear to act.
Let your honorable deeds be an example.
