content.text: You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the Ranger spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Ranger spells. *[Cure Wounds](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/cure-wounds)* and *[Ensnaring Strike](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/ensnaring-strike)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Ranger Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Ranger spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Ranger Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Ranger, your list of prepared spells can include six Ranger spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Ranger feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Ranger spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use a [Druidic Focus](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/druidic-focus) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Ranger spells.

You always have the *[Hunter's Mark](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/hunters-mark)* spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Ranger levels, as shown in the Favored Enemy column of the Ranger Features table.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as [Longbows](srd-5.2/06/weapons/longbow) and [Shortswords](srd-5.2/06/weapons/shortsword).

Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of [Scimitars](srd-5.2/06/weapons/scimitar) and [Longswords](srd-5.2/06/weapons/longsword).
Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits.

content.label: Expertise
content.text: Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise). You gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in that skill.

content.label: Languages
content.text: You know two languages of your choice from the language tables in chapter 2.
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

You gain a Ranger subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Ranger levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Ranger level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 8, 12, and 16.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.

Your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a [Climb Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/climb-speed) and a [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed).
Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise). You gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in those skills.
Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits.

content.label: Temporary Hit Points
content.text: As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can give yourself a number of [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Decrease Exhaustion
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), your [Exhaustion](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/exhaustion) level, if any, decreases by 1.
Taking damage can't break your [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) on Hunter's Mark.

You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can give yourself the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.
Your connection to the forces of nature grants you [Blindsight](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blindsight) with a range of 30 feet.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Dimensional Travel](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-dimensional-travel) is recommended.
The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.
As a Ranger, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Ranger levels. These features are listed in the Ranger Features table.

This section presents the Ranger spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.

Your tenacity can wear down even the most resilient foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage to the target if it's missing any of its [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, that is within the weapon's range, and that you haven't attacked this turn.

You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey. While a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.
[Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks) have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) against you.
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, that creature has [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on all other attack rolls against you this turn.

You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark, you can also deal that spell's extra damage to a different creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.

When you take damage, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to give yourself [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to that damage and any other damage of the same type until the end of the current turn.
You stalk prey in the wilds and elsewhere, using your abilities as a Hunter to protect nature and people everywhere from forces that would destroy them.

content.text: You gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. [Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand) and [Stealth](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/stealth) are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Rogue level 6, you gain [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition, and you don't have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on the attack roll.
The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in chapter 2.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as [Daggers](srd-5.2/06/weapons/dagger) and [Shortbows](srd-5.2/06/weapons/shortbow).

Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of [Scimitars](srd-5.2/06/weapons/scimitar) and [Shortswords](srd-5.2/06/weapons/shortsword).

Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action): [Dash](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dash), [Disengage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disengage), or [Hide](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hide).

You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Rogue level or lower.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you give yourself [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is 0 until the end of the current turn.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Rogue levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
To use this effect, you must have a [Poisoner's Kit](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/poisoners-kit) on your person.
If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition.
Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) without provoking [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks).

You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove 1d6 from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.
If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency).
When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition.
Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or it has the [Unconscious](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unconscious) condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The [Unconscious](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unconscious) target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or it has the [Blinded](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blinded) condition until the end of its next turn.
You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.
Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) against you unless you have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of the Night Spirit](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-the-night-spirit) is recommended.
You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a [D20 Test](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test), you can turn the roll into a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.text: Make a Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check to pick a lock or disarm a trap with [Thieves' Tools](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/thieves-tools) or to pick a pocket.
Take the [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, or take the [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to use a magic item that requires that action.
As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can do one of the following.
You gain a [Climb Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/climb-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed).
You can determine your jump distance using your Dexterity rather than your Strength.
You've trained to get into especially hard-to-reach places, granting you these benefits.

If you have the [Hide](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hide) action's [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition, this attack doesn't end that condition on you if you end the turn behind [Three-Quarters Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) or [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover).
You gain the following Cunning Strike option.
You can attune to up to four magic items at once.
Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll 1d6. On a roll of 6, you use the property without expending the charges.

You can use any *[Spell Scroll](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/spell-scroll)*, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for the spell. If the spell is a cantrip or a level 1 spell, you can cast it reliably. If the scroll contains a higher-level spell, you must first succeed on an Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana)) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell from the scroll. On a failed check, the scroll disintegrates.
You've learned how to maximize use of magic items, granting you the following benefits.

You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) and your second turn at your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) minus 10.

A mix of burglar, treasure hunter, and explorer, you are the epitome of an adventurer. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you gain abilities useful for delving into ruins and getting maximum benefit from the magic items you find there.

content.text: Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. *[Light](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/light)*, *[Prestidigitation](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/prestidigitation)*, *[Shocking Grasp](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/shocking-grasp)*, and *[Sorcerous Burst](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/sorcerous-burst)* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. *[Burning Hands](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/burning-hands)* and *[Detect Magic](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-magic)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use an [Arcane Focus](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/arcane-focus) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Sorcerer spells.

An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

items.text: The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1.
You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

content.text: You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.

content.label: Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points
content.text: You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

content.label: Creating Spell Slots
content.text: As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Sorcerer level you must be to create a slot. You can create a spell slot no higher than level 5.
Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class's description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.

You gain a Sorcerer subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Sorcerer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Sorcerer level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

When you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to activate it.
In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your Metamagic options on each spell you cast.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Dimensional Travel](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-dimensional-travel) is recommended.
While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.
As a Sorcerer, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Sorcerer levels. These features are listed in the Sorcerer Features table.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell's full force. To do so, spend 1 Sorcery Point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell, and it takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that has a range of at least 5 feet, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to double the spell's range. Or when you cast a spell that has a range of Touch, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to make the spell's range 30 feet.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point
When you roll damage for a spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), and you must use the new rolls.
You can use Empowered Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point
When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to double its duration to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

If the affected spell requires [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration), you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on any saving throw you make to maintain that [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration).

content.label: Cost
content.text: 2 Sorcery Points

When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to give one target of the spell [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on saves against the spell.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 2 Sorcery Points

When you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to change the casting time to a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) for this casting. You can't modify a spell in this way if you've already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell on this turn after modifying a spell in this way.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point
If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll.
You can use Seeking Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or Material components, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or that have a cost specified in the spell.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Thunder.

content.label: Cost
content.text: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell, such as *[Charm Person](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/charm-person)*, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to increase the spell's effective level by 1.
The following options are available to your Metamagic feature. The options are presented in alphabetical order.

This section presents the Sorcerer spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.

The magic in your body manifests physical traits of your draconic gift. Your [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.

Parts of you are also covered by dragon-like scales. While you aren't wearing armor, your base [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
Your draconic magic has an affinity with a damage type associated with dragons. Choose one of those types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to that damage type, and when you cast a spell that deals damage of that type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can cause draconic wings to appear on your back. The wings last for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration, you have a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) of 60 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) unless you spend 3 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

You can cast *[Summon Dragon](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/summon-dragon)* without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration). If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

Your innate magic comes from the gift of a dragon. Perhaps an ancient dragon facing death bequeathed some of its magical power to you or your ancestor. You might have absorbed magic from a site infused with dragons' power. Or perhaps you handled a treasure taken from a dragon's hoard that was steeped in draconic power. Or you might have a dragon for an ancestor.

Gain the Warlock's level 1 features, which are listed in the Warlock Features table. See the multiclassing rules in chapter 2 to determine your available spell slots.

content.text: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "Eldritch Invocation Options" section later in this class's description.

content.label: Prerequisites
content.text: If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

content.label: Replacing and Gaining Invocations
content.text: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.
When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.
You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. *[Eldritch Blast](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/eldritch-blast)* and *[Prestidigitation](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/prestidigitation)* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell *Witch Bolt*, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. *[Charm Person](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/charm-person)* and *[Hex](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/hex)* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.

If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Charisma is the spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use an [Arcane Focus](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/arcane-focus) as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Warlock spells.

You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

You gain a Warlock subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Warlock levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Warlock level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Warlock levels 8, 12, and 16.

In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the *[Contact Other Plane](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/contact-other-plane)* spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot to contact your patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Warlock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 13 (level 7 spell), 15 (level 8 spell), and 17 (level 9 spell). You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Fate](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-fate) is recommended.
When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.
As a Warlock, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Warlock levels. These features are listed in the Warlock Features table.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage
Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls.

content.label: Repeatable
content.text: You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

content.text: You can cast *[Mage Armor](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/mage-armor)* on yourself without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock
You can cast *[Levitate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/levitate)* on yourself without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock
You can see normally in [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) and [Darkness](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkness)—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 12+ Warlock
The Extra Attack of your [Thirsting Blade](srd-5.2/03/warlock/eldritch-invocation-options/thirsting-blade) invocation confers two extra attacks rather than one.
You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration).

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target, plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition if it is Huge or smaller.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage
Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level.

content.label: Repeatable
content.text: You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock

You can cast *[False Life](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/false-life)* on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don't roll the die for the [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points); you automatically get the highest number on the die.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock

You can use a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. The connection ends if you don't maintain it in this way.

While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or the other creature's space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock
You can breathe underwater, and you gain a [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed).

You can also cast *[Water Breathing](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/water-breathing)* once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way again when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 9+ Warlock

A new page appears in your Book of Shadows when you conjure it. With your permission, a creature can take an action to write its name on that page, which can contain a number of names equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one name).

When any creature whose name is on the page is reduced to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) but not killed outright, the creature magically drops to 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) instead. Once this magic is triggered, no creature can benefit from it until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).
As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can erase a name on the page by touching it.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock
When you cast *[Find Familiar](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/find-familiar)*, you infuse the summoned familiar with a measure of your eldritch power, granting the creature the following benefits.

content.label: Aerial or Aquatic
content.text: The familiar gains either a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) or a [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) (your choice) of 40 feet.

content.label: Quick Attack
content.text: As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can command the familiar to take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action.

content.label: Necrotic or Radiant Damage
content.text: Whenever the familiar deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can make it deal Necrotic or Radiant damage instead.

content.label: Your Save DC
content.text: If the familiar forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.

content.label: Resistance
content.text: When the familiar takes damage, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to grant it [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) against that damage.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock
You have received knowledge from an elder entity of the multiverse, allowing you to gain one Origin feat of your choice.

content.label: Repeatable
content.text: You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different Origin feat.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 9+ Warlock

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage (your choice) to the creature, and you can expend one of your [Hit Point Dice](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-point-dice) to roll it and regain a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points)).

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock
You can cast *[Disguise Self](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/disguise-self)* without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock
You can cast *[Alter Self](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/alter-self)* without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock
You can cast *[Silent Image](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/silent-image)* without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock

While you're in an area of [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) or [Darkness](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkness), you can cast *[Invisibility](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/invisibility)* on yourself without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock
You can cast *[Jump](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/jump)* on yourself without expending a spell slot.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can conjure a pact weapon in your hand—a Simple or Martial Melee weapon of your choice with which you bond—or create a bond with a magic weapon you touch; you can't bond with a magic weapon if someone else is attuned to it or another Warlock is bonded with it. Until the bond ends, you have proficiency with the weapon, and you can use it as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus).

Whenever you attack with the bonded weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity; and you can cause the weapon to deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage or its normal damage type.

Your bond with the weapon ends if you use this feature's [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) again, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die. A conjured weapon disappears when the bond ends.
You learn the *[Find Familiar](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/find-familiar)* spell and can cast it as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action without expending a spell slot.

When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: [Imp](srd-5.2/14/imp/imp), [Pseudodragon](srd-5.2/14/pseudodragon/pseudodragon), [Quasit](srd-5.2/14/quasit/quasit), [Skeleton](srd-5.2/14/skeletons/skeleton), [Sphinx of Wonder](srd-5.2/14/sphinxes/sphinx-of-wonder), [Sprite](srd-5.2/14/sprite/sprite), or [Venomous Snake](srd-5.2/15/venomous-snake) (see appendix B for the familiar's stat block).

Additionally, when you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction).

Stitching together strands of shadow, you conjure forth a book in your hand at the end of a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). This Book of Shadows (you determine its appearance) contains eldritch magic that only you can access, granting you the benefits below. The book disappears if you conjure another book with this feature or if you die.

content.label: Cantrips and Rituals
content.text: When the book appears, choose three cantrips, and choose two level 1 spells that have the [Ritual](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/ritual) tag. The spells can be from any class's spell list, and they must be spells you don't already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use the book as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus).

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage via an Attack Roll
Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you.

content.label: Repeatable
content.text: You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 5+ Warlock

You gain the Extra Attack feature for your pact weapon only. With that feature, you can attack twice with the weapon instead of once when you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 9+ Warlock
You can cast *[Arcane Eye](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/arcane-eye)* without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 7+ Warlock
You can cast *[Speak with Dead](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/speak-with-dead)* without expending a spell slot.

content.label: Prerequisite
content.text: Level 15+ Warlock
You have [Truesight](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/truesight) with a range of 30 feet.
Eldritch Invocation options appear in alphabetical order.

This section presents the Warlock spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.
The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

When you reduce an enemy to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), you gain [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1 [Temporary Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points)). You also gain this benefit if someone else reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points).

You can call on your fiendish patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add 1d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), but you can use it no more than once per roll. You regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

Choose one damage type, other than Force, whenever you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the target disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. The target takes 8d10 Psychic damage if it isn't a Fiend, and it has the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition until the end of your next turn, when it returns to the space it previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest) unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

Your pact draws on the Lower Planes, the realms of perdition. You might forge a bargain with a demon lord such as Demogorgon or Orcus; an archdevil; or a pit fiend, balor, yugoloth, or night hag that is especially mighty. That patron's aims are evil—the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you—and your path is defined by the extent to which you strive against those aims.

content.text: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class's description.

content.label: Cantrips
content.text: You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. *[Light](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/light)*, *[Mage Hand](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/mage-hand)*, and *[Ray of Frost](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/ray-of-frost)* are recommended. Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

content.label: Spellbook
content.text: Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting *[Identify](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/identify)*. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. *[Detect Magic](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-magic)*, *[Feather Fall](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/feather-fall)*, *[Mage Armor](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/mage-armor)*, *[Magic Missile](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/magic-missile)*, *[Sleep](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/sleep)*, and *[Thunderwave](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/thunderwave)* are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

content.label: Spell Slots
content.text: The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
content.text: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

content.label: Changing Your Prepared Spells
content.text: Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

content.label: Spellcasting Ability
content.text: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: You can use an [Arcane Focus](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/arcane-focus) or your spellbook as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Wizard spells.

The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a *[Spell Scroll](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/spell-scroll)*, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

content.label: Copying a Spell into the Book
content.text: When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

content.label: Copying the Book
content.text: You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

You can cast any spell as a [Ritual](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/ritual) if that spell has the [Ritual](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/ritual) tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: [Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana), [History](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/history), [Investigation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/investigation), [Medicine](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/medicine), [Nature](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/nature), or [Religion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/religion). You have [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in the chosen skill.

You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](srd-5.2/05/general-feats/ability-score-improvement) feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

Whenever you finish a [Short Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest), you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.
Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Spell Recall](srd-5.2/05/epic-boon-feats/boon-of-spell-recall) is recommended.

Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.
As a Wizard, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Wizard levels. These features are listed in the Wizard Features table.

This section presents the Wizard spell list. The spells are organized by spell level and then alphabetized, and each spell's school of magic is listed. In the Special column, C means the spell requires Concentration, R means it's a Ritual, and M means it requires a specific Material component.
Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.
You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you take 2d12 Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) and [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity).
Each time you use this feature again before finishing a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12.

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.
